one_month_reasoning: In the window: the Q1 FY27 print on Wed 2026-11-04 after the close (guide revenue $2.2-2.4B, non-GAAP EPS 1.85-2.05; Street 1.97/$2.30B) and the Q2 guide. The 8-quarter record is 8 of 8 revenue quarters above the midpoint (median +3.3%) and 8 of 8 EPS at or above it (median +8.7%), and InP output was guided to double by the end of this quarter, so a beat and a Q2 guide near $2.6B are likely; that is largely expected (whisper ~2.03-2.05). Offsetting: post-print reactions have been mixed (August beat was followed by a fall from ~379 to ~280 in two weeks; May rose), the October slide of -38% was a sector rotation with no company news (24/7 Wall St 10-15) that could continue with AI-hardware sentiment, and the Marvell-Lumentum deal adds noise. Distribution: lognormal around a median of ~213 (+1%, a small post-beat drift and reversal after a sharp fall) with a 25% one-month sigma (89% annual / 3.5, which already includes event days). Also in the window: the 2026-11-18 annual meeting (no value event) and NVIDIA's late-November results (read-across).

fair_value.method: Driver-led quarterly build (D&C = AI-cluster optics market x capture; Industrial revenue x margin) valued with two P/E legs at the horizon: 0.7 x 19.5x the build's NTM EPS ~14.59 (= 290.81) and 0.3 x 19.5x a mid-cycle EPS 11.96 (= 239.56), both including +$6.34/share of probability-weighted Marvell-Lumentum share shift beyond the NTM year.

downside.story: P10: AI optics digestion in CY2027-28 (the standing capex file's low case has 2028 customer capex below 2027) plus share loss to Chinese 1.6T module makers and the Marvell bundle (share-shift low variant, run-rate op income -84 instead of +136): D&C capture -22% (FY28 D&C ~9.7B, +7%), D&C margin -2.5pt (back to the FY25-26 24-25% band with under-absorbed new InP fabs), Industrial -8% (semicap turn), and the multiple derates 6 turns to ~13.5x, where COHR traded on FY24 trough earnings. Mid-cycle EPS -25%.

base.story: Median: Q1 FY27 lands at ~$2.37B / EPS 2.07; InP capacity doubling then more than doubling lets D&C reach >$3B quarters by Q4 FY27 and ~12.5B in FY28 (+37%); FY28 revenue 14.4B (Street 14.41B), EPS 13.7; capex ~2.2B in FY27 keeps net debt ~1.8B at the horizon; the stock re-rates from ~15.3x our FY28 EPS (13.71) today to 19.5x NTM, a peer-anchored multiple, partly discounted for mid-cycle margins.

upside.story: P90: InP capacity more than doubles on time in CY2027, CPO light sources and OCS add on top (management TAMs >$15B and >$4B), FY28 D&C ~14.3B (+57%, at the market's pace) and the share-shift high variant starts to show; D&C margin +1.5pt toward the >42% gross-margin target; multiple +5 turns to ~24.5x (CIEN/GLW level). Mid-cycle EPS +15%.

comps_summary.peer_range: Whole-company NTM P/E 18.9x-32.4x (FN, AAOI, CRDO, MTSI; median 20.9x). Context excluded from the median: CIEN 28.4x, GLW 29.5x, ALAB 56.4x, LITE 27.7x and MRVL 31.5x (deal-driven); Industrial segment-only IPGP 32.9x, MKSI 12.3x, NOVT 35.1x (median 32.9x). No NTM EV/EBITDA consensus in the table.
comps_summary.own_multiple_basis: 210.41 / 10.62 company non-GAAP NTM EPS (Zacks NTM 9.62 + 4 x 0.25 basis gap); 21.9x on the Zacks basis
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19.5x company non-GAAP NTM EPS at the horizon: 0.93x the 20.9x median, inside the 18.9x-32.4x range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued. The k=0.8 shrink keeps most of COHR's small discount (own 19.8x vs 20.9x); a further -0.5 turn carries COHR-specific post-horizon risks (CPO shifting value from pluggables, Chinese 1.6T price pressure, Marvell DSP dependence). COHR's larger Industrial exposure and lower margins than CRDO/MTSI justify sitting below the median; its vertical integration (own InP) and NVIDIA LTA support not being lower.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 4 whole-company peers only (FN, AAOI, CRDO, MTSI). No more genuine ones: LITE and MRVL are deal-pegged since 2026-11-02, Innolight/Eoptolink are China-listed (excluded by rule), CIEN and GLW match under 25% of COHR revenue, ALAB has a different model; IPGP/MKSI/NOVT are Industrial segment-only (~13%).

thesis_break_reason: At $145 COHR would trade at ~10.6x our FY28 company-basis EPS (13.7) and ~14.7x FY27 (9.87): a level that only makes sense if FY28 earnings are about to fall 25-35% (an AI optics digestion, a lost hyperscaler/NVIDIA program, or a capacity-ramp failure at the 6-inch InP fabs). The 52-week low 123.75 was set before the FY26 ramp on ~5.6 EPS; a return toward it with FY27 booked out would signal a fundamental break, not volatility. Watch: a Q2 guide below the ~$2.37B Q1 actual, inventory rising faster than revenue again (FY26 +80%), or LTA cancellations.

reasoning: Primary-document lane. Started from the thread's proposed quarterly driver set (D&C = LightCounting AI-cluster optics x capture, D&C margin, Industrial revenue x margin) and checked each driver against the filings. Driver views: dc_capture kept through FY27 and lifted 4% in FY28-29 because the Q4 FY26 slides and call say InP output doubles by end CY2026 and more than doubles again by end CY2027, FY27 is almost fully booked with orders into CY2028 and LTAs to the end of the decade; this puts FY28 revenue at 14.4B, in line with the Street 14.41B. dc_margin, ind_rev and ind_margin kept (consistent with the May 2025 target model: >42% GM, 18% opex, >24% operating margin, and the 10-K segment notes). Biggest primary-document change: capex. The set had 12% of FY27 revenue; Q4 FY26 capex was $556M (27% of revenue) with a further sequential rise guided, so we use 20%/13%/10% and D&A 3.5-3.9%, which raises horizon net debt to ~1.8B (no financing needed: 1.99B cash and ST investments, debt matures FY30-31). Guidance record from eight Ex.99.1 releases (Q4 FY24-Q3 FY26 guides vs next-quarter actuals): revenue 8/8 above midpoint (median +3.3%), GM inside 7/8 (median +0.5%), EPS 8/8 at or above (median +8.7%); the FY26 proxy shows the internal revenue target 6,370 beaten at 7,288 and adjusted EBITDA 1,550 vs 1,745. We sit inside the revenue guide (2,370), at the guide-implied margin, EPS 2.07 just above the top. Valuation: P/E is the only multiple the peer table supports (no NTM EV/EBITDA). Whole-company peers are only FN, AAOI, CRDO, MTSI (median 20.9x); COHR's own 19.8x (company basis) shrinks with k=0.8 to 20.0x, less 0.5 turn for CPO and China price risk = 19.5x. 0.3 of the weight on a mid-cycle 20.5% margin answers the playbook's peak-margin warning. Marvell-Lumentum: accept the appraisal's base capture (both suppliers sold out; LITE guides +26% q/q), book p 0.75 x post-NTM run-rate as +1,299 ($6.34/share). Not driver-linked: the mid-cycle EPS (stated) and the Marvell adjustment. Scenarios move the drivers: downside capture -22%, D&C margin -2.5pt, Industrial -8%, multiple -6 turns (the capex file's low case, 89% realised vol, the -52% drawdown from 440 in five months); upside capture +15%, margin +1.5pt, multiple +5. Research was limited to filings and two call recaps (no full transcript reachable); the stock's October slide was a sector rotation with no company news.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led quarterly set (Q1 FY2026-Q4 FY2029, actual = 4) started from the thread's proposed set (source 22): D&C = LightCounting AI-cluster Ethernet optics market x dc_capture (+ lite_shift hook), D&C margin, Industrial revenue and margin, corporate constant. Basis: company non-GAAP operating income (ex SBC, amortization, restructuring); SBC counted once through share dilution (+1%/yr). Value carried by two P/E legs: 0.7 on the build's own horizon NTM EPS at 19.5x and 0.3 on a mid-cycle EPS (20.5% margin) at 19.5x, plus a probability-weighted Marvell-Lumentum adjustment beyond the NTM year. No DCF (policy). No SOTP leg: Industrial is ~13% of FY28 revenue and its segment-only peers (IPGP 32.9x, MKSI 12.3x, NOVT 35.1x) are too dispersed to move the value; a SOTP at 20x for Industrial changes the target by under 1%. Driven share of revenue 100%. Changes vs the set: dc_capture FY28-29 +4%; capex 20/13/10% of revenue (set 12/10/9%) on the Q4 FY26 $556M quarter and the guided sequential rise; D&A 3.5/3.7/3.9%; sbc_treatment dilution.

model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) dc_capture +4% FY28-29 vs the set: about +3% on the research target (12m). (2) Capex 20% of FY27 revenue vs the set's 12%: lowers FCF by ~0.9B and raises horizon net debt, about -$4/share via the bridge and interest. (3) Exit P/E 19.5x: k=0.8 shrink gives 20.0x; -0.5 turn for COHR-specific post-horizon risks (CPO content shift, Chinese module price pressure). (4) Mid-cycle leg weight 0.3 at 20.5% margin: if dropped, target about +5%. (5) Peer basis: COHR's Zacks-basis EPS runs ~0.22-0.27/qtr below company non-GAAP (about after-tax SBC); measured on the Zacks basis COHR's own NTM P/E is 21.9x vs a 20.9x median -> 21.7x Zacks basis = ~19.5x on company basis, the same answer. No financing event above 20%: cash + ST investments 1,987 and a revolver cover the FY27 FCF gap of ~0.7B (no ATM or shelf found).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued. The k=0.8 shrink keeps most of COHR's small discount (own 19.8x vs 20.9x); a further -0.5 turn carries COHR-specific post-horizon risks (CPO shifting value from pluggables, Chinese 1.6T price pressure, Marvell DSP dependence). COHR's larger Industrial exposure and lower margins than CRDO/MTSI justify sitting below the median; its vertical integration (own InP) and NVIDIA LTA support not being lower.

No more genuine ones: LITE and MRVL are deal-pegged since 2026-11-02, Innolight/Eoptolink are China-listed (excluded by rule), CIEN and GLW match under 25% of COHR revenue, ALAB has a different model; IPGP/MKSI/NOVT are Industrial segment-only (~13%).
